Who it's for

# Wherever you work, the hard part is the same: getting every team to deliver what it agreed

Plannerly is for the person running information management - BIM manager, information manager or digital lead - at owners, contractors, architects, consultants and universities. Pick your kind of organisation to see your ISO 19650 jobs in the order you'll meet them, with proof from teams like yours.

[Start free](https://app.plannerly.com/sign-up) [Pick your kind of organisation](https://plannerly.com/for/#organisations)

Free plan, no card. Everyone you invite joins free.

## Who Plannerly is for: your questions, answered

Who is Plannerly for?

The person running information management on construction projects, whatever their title says - BIM manager, information manager, BIM coordinator, digital lead or VDC manager - and the teams they work with. They work at owners and clients, contractors, architects and engineers, consultancies and universities, in nearly 150,000 teams across 100+ countries. [Pick your kind of organisation](https://plannerly.com/for/#organisations), or [see every case study](https://plannerly.com/uses/).

My organisation is more than one of these. Which page is mine?

Pick the role you play on the project in front of you. A design-and-build contractor leading the delivery team reads [the contractors' page](https://plannerly.com/for/contractors/); the same organisation's design team reads [the architects' page](https://plannerly.com/for/architects/). The jobs are the same everywhere - only the order and the emphasis change. [Every use case](https://plannerly.com/use-cases/).

What does ISO 19650 call each kind of organisation?

The owner or client is the appointing party. The organisation leading delivery for an appointment - often the main contractor or the lead designer - is the lead appointed party, and each organisation appointed under it is an appointed party, made up of one or more task teams. The free lesson on [ISO 19650 roles and responsibilities](https://plannerly.com/courses/expert/lesson/iso-19650-roles-and-responsibilities-explained/) explains each, and [ISO 19650-2](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:19650:-2:ed-1:v1:en) sets them out.

Do I need to know ISO 19650 first?

No. Each page starts from the problem, and every job links the free lesson for its steps. If you'd like the basics first, the free courses come with a certificate each, from Level 1 BIM Management Basics to Level 3 ISO 19650 Expert, rated 4.9 out of 5 from thousands of ratings. [Start the free training](https://plannerly.com/training/), and [ISO 19650 on one page](https://plannerly.com/iso-19650-pdf/).

Do the teams I work with have to pay?

No. Everyone you invite joins at no cost to them. On Pro, editors and viewers are unlimited, so every company on the project can work on its own part; on Free you're the editor and everyone you invite can view and comment. [Compare the plans](https://plannerly.com/pricing/).

Is there a version for universities?

Yes. Plannerly is free for official universities and education programmes, with a guest lecture, a hands-on assignment and free courses with certificates. [Plannerly for universities and colleges](https://plannerly.com/for/education/).
